notes: Only packet 147_scan088 and shared workflow/rules/notation were used. The source page, both native halves, and all 12 created crops were visually inspected. No OCR, external sources or TeX compilation was used.

All crop boxes refer to the original 1692 × 2358 image. The NB crop uses box [15,315,445,1640], rotated −57 degrees with white expansion before enlargement. Other crops are unrotated. Pillow LANCZOS enlargement, autocontrast and mild UnsharpMask were used only for legibility.

The NB rectangle also contains partial adjacent body strokes at its edges. They belong to the separately transcribed main text and are not extra margin words. The long margin is read in its own slanting baseline order.
The top 43 is dark and matches the main writing. The lower 87 is markedly paler and differently placed; it is preserved as margin foliation without asserting authorial ownership.

The page states condition (Simp) as a finite-power-set description of the ordered quotients; it then names the maximal proper quotients and uses the complementary subset A_G minus C to name G/C. These are reported assertions, not independently proved here.

The category glyph in (123) is M-like, whereas the later Ob expression contains the distinct curly G form. The transcription preserves that visible variation. Mathematical expectations did not replace the clear first glyph.

The NB asks for the application of this axiomatization to relative analytic multiplicités and mentions a quotient of a twisted integer lattice. The old types of multiplicités remain cancelled, and the final old word remains uncertain.

The opening parenthesis after normaux in NB has no written closing partner. The dot groups after normaux and at the end of tel are retained as ellipses; no closing parenthesis or final explanatory wording is supplied.

The main extension statement contains a full stop after the lattice before the parenthetical en fait. The bottom clause has no external full stop after its closing parenthesis; only the abbreviation point in quelc. is written.

H's editorial page note and its note about the M-like category glyph are not manuscript text. Its uncertain readings of isomorphe, donc, d'autant, montrer, une and non pas agree in wording with the ink; certainty-only improvements are not counted as separate textual errors.

The new uncertainty on cancelled minimaux is not a changed word against C. Diagram (124) likewise adds local geometry uncertainty against C; H's definite ordinary arrow is recorded as a differing endpoint reading at low confidence, without claiming the harpoon/dash alternative is settled.
The live adjective maximaux is preferred from the visible x-shaped internal stroke; its old cancelled companion is less legible. Both are included together in the mandatory blind box.
Reader B performed no proof checking. The main reader separately supplied the targeted finite-poset check recorded below; no independent re-proof, computation or formal certificate is claimed.

Main-reader mathematical check: under the page's stated reverse-inclusion identification, nonempty subsets C represent proper quotients. A C with at least two elements has a proper nonempty subset above it; a singleton has none. Hence maximal proper quotients correspond to singleton subsets. This is consistent with the written replacement maximaux, but does not decide its ink and does not prove the simplex axiom.

check_events.outcome: Main reader verified this finite-poset implication under the page's stated identification: in the reverse-inclusion order on nonempty subsets C, maximal elements are exactly singletons. If C has at least two elements, a proper nonempty subset is above it; a singleton has no such subset. This check does not prove the simplex axiom and was not used to override the ink.
